# Registered KERNEL (type-checking) ceilings, milliseconds.
# Generated by scripts/kernel_cost.py --register on the P0 baseline.
# Ceiling = max(measured x 3.0, 50ms): below the floor,
# timing noise dominates and a ratio would fail on a loaded machine.
#
# ⚠️ Tests.Coverage was RAISED from 777 by P1 BATCH 3, deliberately and not by
# --register (which would have loosened every other line at the same time).
# The module went 378ms -> 1960ms, and 1292ms of that is ONE theorem:
# `mem_dest_claims_are_backed`, which reads the table's SHAPES column — prose,
# up to 75 characters a row — as a character list in the kernel.  It is the gate
# that caught a false `m,r (q)` coverage claim that had stood since batch 1 with
# a reassuring comment beside it.  The cheaper design (a Bool field the renderer
# turns into text) was considered and rejected: it makes the prose unable to
# UNDER-claim while leaving it free to OVER-claim, which is the direction that
# actually failed.  A gate on the artifact costs more than a gate on a shadow of
# it, and this is what the difference costs.  See docs/DECISIONS.md D15.
#
# ⭐⭐ P1 BATCH 14 STOPPED RAISING IT AND CHANGED ITS UNITS.  See D38.
# Tests.Coverage's kernel cost is LINEAR IN THE COVERAGE TABLE, which grows
# every batch by construction, so an absolute ceiling on it must be raised every
# batch — and a gate relaxed on schedule is not a gate.  Batch 10 measured 2.4x
# headroom and wrote that there was "room to do this properly rather than under
# pressure"; batches 11-13 did not, and batch 14 arrived at 1.09x.  The ceiling
# is now PER ROW, multiplied by the kernel-pinned `rosterSize`.
#
# ⛔ AND THE ABSOLUTE CEILING PROVABLY MISSED THE REGRESSION THE NEW ONE CATCHES.
# Batch 13 added one theorem costing 12 400ms — measured by batch 14, which also
# found the handed-on figure for it (5 800ms) was low by more than a factor of
# two.  The module went ~90ms/row to 293ms/row, a 3.2x jump in cost per row, and
# the absolute ceiling did NOT fire (17 900 against 19 560).  A per-row ceiling
# at this headroom fires on exactly that.
#
# The registered figure GRANDFATHERS batch 13's theorem rather than pretending
# it is not there: 293ms/row measured x 1.6.  The headroom is tighter than the
# 3.0 used for absolute lines because ordinary GROWTH is now divided out and
# only noise (measured at ~3% across three runs) and real regressions remain.
#
# ⭐ AND Tests.Nonvacuity DELIBERATELY KEEPS AN ABSOLUTE CEILING — it is the
# counterpoint that makes the rule above a rule rather than a habit.  It went
# OVER on the same day (81.5ms against 71) because batch 14 added seventeen
# theorems, four of which draw a 64-bit undefined DESTINATION and so evaluate
# `Oracle.drawVal` sixty-four deep inside a `decide`.  That growth is NOT
# structural: this module grows only when a batch deliberately writes new
# obligations, which is exactly the moment a head should be made to state the
# cost out loud.  A per-row ceiling here would divide out the only signal there
# is.  RAISED to 81.5 x 3.0 = 245 by hand, not by --register.
#
# ⚠️ Measured on an IDLE machine (81.8 / 81.4 across two runs).  The first
# reading was 94ms and was taken while the 21-minute selftest was running; a
# ceiling registered from that number would have been ~15% loose for ever.
X86.Basic 163
X86.Coverage 50
X86.Flags 50
X86.Memory 50
X86.Oracle 50
X86.Semantics 50
X86.Serialize 50
X86.State 50
X86.Syntax 124
X86.Theorems 540
X86.Value 61
X86 50

Tests.Anchors 801
Tests.Coverage @perRow 470.0
Tests.Nonvacuity 245
